text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: high-latency + instance crashes in us-west continuous-batcher pool (sev=2)

alex: seeing a steady p95 latency climb across the continuous-batcher group, peaking at 18s. multiple containers OOMed then restarted. CPU fine, GPU mem exhausted.

sophia: copying last OOM log from node gpu-uw2-31:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc: XXX] CUDA_ERROR_MEMORY_ALLOCATION: out of memory
2026-03-15 10:03:22,123 runtime: kvcache_prefetch: growth to 47GB for model gptx-16k-quant causing eviction thrash
last_alloc: 44.8GB requested, available: 2.3GB
```

alex: this looks like the KV-prefetch growth bug resurfacing (batch accumulation doesn't prune). starting mitigation: scale batcher workers to 0.6x and enable immediate-kv-drop gate.

ryan: on it. I'm flipping dynamic-batch-limit -> 32 from 128 for continuous-batcher in us-west-prod. will also push a hotfix that disables prefetch for long-seqs.

marie: FYI customer-ops reports increased error rate to a few enterprise customers (chat endpoints queued, timeouts). customer-ops pinged affected tenants. need an impact assessment.

alex: timeline so far: 10:02 first p95 spike, 10:03 first GPU OOM and container restart, 10:04 subsequent node flaps as restarts trigger prefetch rehydration, 10:06 cascading batch growth on nodes that rejoined.

sophia: applying 2 actions now:
1) deploy-bot, rollback continuous-batcher prefetch flag to safe-default (off) -> deploy?
2) route traffic from continuous-batcher to cpu-fallback-pool for non-latency-critical customers

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted. Rolling config change: continuous_prefetch_enabled=false on us-west cluster. Canary: gpu-uw2-15.

alex: while deploy rolls, doing manual drain of gpu-uw2-31 (the worst offender) and force-kill jobs that still hold KV.

ryan: drain in progress: `kubectl cordon gpu-uw2-31 && kubectl drain gpu-uw2-31 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sophia: note — draining causes short spike in queue depth as requests are redistributed. to prevent cascade, I'm enabling token-based ingress rate-limiting for the group: 10 reqs/s per org for 10m.

customer-ops: Notifying top impacted customer (figma-similar) now with ETA 15m for mitigation. They see ~30% error rate for chat endpoints.

ryan: hotfix applied: prefetch disabled, batch cap lowered. Observability: p95 dropped from 18s -> 2.4s on canary within 90s. OOMs stopped on canary.

alex: good. rolling to remaining nodes in 3 batches to avoid waves. will keep the rate-limit in place until cluster stabilizes.

sophia: adding temporary A/B fallback: route 20% of high-throughput traffic to ded-pool-small (lower-cost but stable) to absorb load while we validate.

marie: customers: figma-similar acknowledged, asked for postmortem and SLA credit calc. Logged ticket INC-2026-1783.

ryan: one weirdness — we saw a single node (gpu-uw2-42) that didn't respect kvcache trim on restart, ended up refilling to 60GB again. grabbed gcore and heap stats. Suspect race in prefetch cancellation handler.

alex: marking for eng-runtime: @sophia @ryan please escalate to eng-runtime and eng-ml teams. Put a canary test that simulates rapid reconnects with long-seq requests.

sophia: creating a short-term alert rule: if kvcache size > 30GB on any batcher pod -> auto-disable prefetch on that pod and cycle process. Will PR by EOD.

deploy-bot: config roll complete across us-west continuous-batcher. No new OOMs observed in last 5m.

customer-ops: customers updated. Some report partial recovery. figma-similar still sees degraded throughput for heavy sessions but errors dropped to ~5%.

alex: moving to handoff: oncall->eng-runtime. Last checks: p95 ~2.1s, errors trending down. Keeping rate-limits and ded-pool routing for 30m.

ryan: handoff notes for eng-runtime: probable bug in kv-prefetch cancel/trim path causing unbounded KV growth when node restarts interleave with inflight prefetch. Repro steps included. Logs and gcore uploaded to /var/logs/incidents/2790012345/

sophia: actions for eng-runtime post-handoff:
- urgent: patch prefetch cancellation race
- medium: add pod-level kvcache soft-limit with enforced trim
- long: add end-to-end sim tests for reconnect + long-seq prefetch

alex: tagging postmortem owner: marie. Drafting initial timeline and customer impact numbers. Please keep updates in this thread.

marie: I'll open postmortem doc and include mitigation timeline, customer impact, SLA calc, and follow-ups. ETA 24h for initial draft.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity downgraded to sev=3. Please follow up with eng-runtime for root cause and eng-sre for monitoring hardening.

sophia: one final note — we should consider a global guardrail: if any continuous-batcher node OOMs twice within 10m, automatically divert its traffic to ded-pool until manually verified.

alex: agreed. That should be in the SRE runbook for batcher incidents. Thanks everyone.

marie: closing handoff. Next: collect logs, assign eng-runtime owner, and schedule RCA.

customer-ops: will reopen if customer impact increases. thanks for the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
